faq.a: A two-day, overnight destination hackathon at Athirappilly Falls in Kerala, organised under DELTA × DATARA’27 by Christ College of Engineering (Autonomous), Dept. of CSE (Data Science).
Proposed for 15–16 January 2027 at Athirappilly, Kerala. Dates and venue are subject to confirmation, and everyone who registers interest will be emailed if anything changes.
Teams of exactly two students. Five teams are selected at Christ College and fifteen more through an open call for other institutions. The exact eligibility rules are in the draft rules.
Yes. Tick “I need a partner” on the form and we will try to match you with another solo participant. Matching is not guaranteed.

faq.q: How are the twenty teams chosen?
faq.a: Five from the campus round and fifteen from the open call, using a defined evaluation that will be published before the call opens.
To be confirmed. This page will be updated, and registrants will be told first.
The proposed plan is buses from Christ College, Irinjalakuda, at 06:30 on Day 1. Travel for teams from other institutions will be confirmed. See the Venue page for distances.

faq.q: Where will we sleep and eat?
faq.a: The plan includes base-camp check-in with beds, chai, dinner and an overnight build. Exact arrangements will be confirmed in the participant guide.
A laptop and charger, your college ID, a headlamp or torch for the night build, a water bottle and any hardware for your idea. A final list comes with the participant guide.
No. The ride is proposed for the finalist teams and is subject to operational confirmation.
The awards programme is still being planned. See the Prizes page.
Only what the registration form asks for is collected, for event communication. See the privacy notice.
See the Contact page. Contact details are published there once they are confirmed.

items: Teams have exactly two members. Nobody can be on more than one team.
Participants must be currently enrolled students at a recognised institution (to be confirmed by the organisers).
Twenty teams take part: five selected at Christ College and fifteen through the open call.
Start the project at the event. Bring ideas, not finished code.
Open-source libraries, public APIs and public datasets are allowed. List them in your project README.
Any code written before the event must be declared and shown in the repository history.
AI coding assistants are allowed if you say how you used them in the README.
On Day 2 at 10:00 every team demos to the jury. Five teams advance to the finale.
Teams are scored on the published criteria. The jury’s decision is final.
A working demo is expected. Slides alone do not qualify.
Your team keeps ownership of what it builds.
The organisers may show demos, screenshots and team names to promote the event, with credit.
Follow instructions from staff around water, the falls and the cable car.
The ride is proposed for finalists and is subject to operational confirmation.
Anyone who endangers themselves or others may be asked to leave.
Plagiarism, submitting someone else’s work, breaking the code of conduct or tampering with other teams’ projects.

venue_notes: The main falls drop about 24 m on the Chalakudy River in the Western Ghats.
The proposed plan is an organised bus from Christ College, Irinjalakuda, on Day 1 at 06:30.
Nearest railway station: Chalakudy, roughly 30 km away. Nearest airport: Cochin International, roughly 55 km away. These distances are approximate; check them before you book anything.
